stm32-an2557-p0007-figure-00001.luna:
Figure 1 is a flowchart of the IAP driver.

Visible flowchart text and logic:

- **Start**
  - Leads to decision: **“Push-button is pressed?”**
    - **No**: routed to **Switch to user program**
      - **Switch to user program**
      - **User application software**
    - **Yes**:
      - **Initialize the STM32F10xxx USART**
      - **Display the IAP main menu**
      - Decision: **“Download or upload or switch or disable write-protection?”**

- From the IAP main-menu decision:
  - **Download**
    - **Receive a binary file**
    - Decision: **“Success”**
      - **No**: **Display the error message “Failed to receive the file”**
      - **Yes**: **Program the Flash**
        - Decision: **“All data programmed successfully?”**
          - **No**: **Display the error message “Verification failed”**
          - **Yes**: **Display the name and size of received file**
    - The download result/error paths are routed back toward the IAP main-menu flow.
  - **Upload**
    - **Transmit image of the device internal Flash**
    - Decision: **“Success”**
      - **No**: **Display the error message “Error has occured”**
      - **Yes**: routed back toward the IAP main-menu flow.
  - **Flash protection**
    - **Disable the write protection**
    - **System reset generation**
    - Routed through the reset loop back to **Start**.
  - **Switch to user program**
    - **Switch to user program**
    - **User application software**

Other visible labels and markers:

- Decision branches are labeled **Yes** and **No**.
- The flowchart uses rectangular process/output boxes and diamond-shaped decision boxes.
- The figure includes a routed return path along the left and bottom edges for returning from IAP operations to the menu flow.
- The spelling shown in the figure is exactly **“Error has occured”**.

stm32-an2557-p0012-table-00001.luna:
**Table 1. STM32F10xxx IAP implementation**

The table has six columns: a device/family column; three **Firmware** columns; and two **Hardware** columns.

**Firmware column descriptions:**
1. “The IAP program is located at 0x8000000. The Flash routines (program/erase) are executed from the Flash memory. The size of this program is about 12 Kbytes and programmed on:”
2. “The user application (image to be loaded with the IAP) will be programmed starting from address 0x8003000(1). The maximum size of the image to be loaded is:”
3. “The image is uploaded with the IAP from the STM32F10xxx internal Flash. The maximum size of the image to be uploaded is:”

**Hardware column descriptions:**
- “Push-button (active level: low)”
- “USART used”

| Device | IAP program placement | Maximum image size / user application | Maximum image uploaded from internal Flash | Push-button | USART used |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Medium-density devices (STM3210B-EVAL)** | page 0 to page 11 | 116 Kbytes (page 12 - page 127) | 116 Kbytes (page 12 - page 127) | Key pushbutton connected to pin PB.09 | USART1 |
| **High-density devices (STM3210E-EVAL)** | page 0 to page 5 | 500 Kbytes (page 6 - page 255) | 500 Kbytes (page 6 - page 255) | Key pushbutton connected to pin PG.08 | USART1 |
| **Connectivity line devices (STM3210C-EVAL)** | page 0 to page 5 | 244 Kbytes (page 6 - page 127) | 244 Kbytes (page 6 - page 127) | Key pushbutton connected to pin PB.09 | USART2 (Tx/Rx pins remapped) |
| **Medium-density value line devices (STM32100B-EVAL)** | page 0 to page 11 | 116 Kbytes (page 12 - page 127) | 116 Kbytes (page 12 - page 127) | Key pushbutton connected to pin PB.09 | USART1 |
| **XL-density devices (STM3210E-EVAL)** | page 0 to page 5 | 1012 Kbytes (page 6 - page 512) | 1012 Kbytes (page 6 - page 512) | Key pushbutton connected to pin PG.08 | USART1 |
| **High-density value line devices (STM32100E-EVAL)** | page 0 to page 5 | 500 Kbytes (page 6 - page 255) | 500 Kbytes (page 6 - page 255) | Key pushbutton connected to pin PG.08 | USART1 |

The user-application address includes footnote marker **(1)** after `0x8003000`; the footnote text is not visible in the provided crop.
